title: A small presenting site representing a prescribed topos object and its slice
statement: Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos [def-weil-pbc-topos] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $A$ be an object of $\mathcal E$. There are a small site $\mathcal C$ with finite limits and subcanonical topology (every representable presheaf is a sheaf), an equivalence of topoi $e:\mathcal E\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, and an object $U\in\mathcal C$ with $e(A)\cong h_U$. With the localized topology on $\mathcal C/U$, there is an equivalence $\mathcal E/A\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)$ under which the slice geometric inverse image $H\mapsto(H\times A\to A)$ corresponds to restriction $F\mapsto F|_U$. Here $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)$ and a family in $\mathcal C/U$ covers precisely when its underlying family covers in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 03CI (lemma-topos-good-site), clauses (1), (3), (5), applied to the singleton family {A}; Tag 04GZ (lemma-localize-topos), statement and proof identifying Sh(C/U) with Sh(C)/h_U and inverse image with restriction.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-topos], choose a $\mathcal V$-small sieve-site presentation $b:\mathcal E\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D,J;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$. Apply [lem-trf-sieve-sheaves-covering-site] to $(\mathcal D,J)$, obtaining a small covering-family site $\mathcal S$ and an equivalence $q:\mathcal E\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$. Put $B=q(A)$. This application uses only the smallness and sieve-topology hypotheses actually supplied by the topos definition; no pullbacks in $\mathcal D$ have been assumed.

source.place: Tag 03CI (lemma-topos-good-site), reduction to a site presentation; arbitrary-sieve starting convention handled by the cited replacement lemma.

proof.text: Construct the underlying category of the desired site. In $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$ let $\mathcal C_0$ be the full subcategory on $B$, the terminal singleton sheaf, and all $h_s^\#$ for $s\in\mathcal S$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Given its set of objects, form $\mathcal C_{n+1}$ by adjoining one fibre product for every cospan in $\mathcal C_n$, retaining all earlier objects. These fibre products and the terminal object exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. The natural transformations between two sheaves form a subset of the product over the $\mathcal V$-small set of objects $s$ of the sets of maps between their $\mathcal V$-small section sets. Hence all Hom sets are $\mathcal V$-small; each stage has only a $\mathcal V$-small set of cospans, and $\mathcal C=\bigcup_{n\geq0}\mathcal C_n$ is $\mathcal V$-small [def-weil-size-convention]. Any cospan in $\mathcal C$ occurs at some finite stage, so its chosen pullback lies in the next stage. Fullness transfers its universal property to $\mathcal C$. Together with the terminal singleton this gives finite limits: products are pullbacks over the terminal object, and the equalizer of $f,g:X\to Y$ is the pullback of $(f,g):X\to Y\times Y$ along the diagonal $Y\to Y\times Y$. Take $U=B$ as an object of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 03CI (lemma-topos-good-site), proof: iterative full-subcategory closure; only finite limits are needed here, so closure under subsheaves is unnecessary. Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-subcategory-comparison] to the full subcategory $\mathcal C\subset\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$. Its three hypotheses hold: the objects form a set, all sheafified representables belong already to $\mathcal C_0$, and it is closed under fibre products by step 2. Thus the epimorphic-family topology makes $\mathcal C$ a small subcanonical site, and $N:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ is the equivalence with $N(F)(V)=\operatorname{Hom}(V,F)$. Set $e=Nq$. The same cited statement gives $N(B)=h_U$, so $e(A)\cong h_U$. An equivalence of categories is an equivalence of topoi: its inverse and unit/counit give an adjunction, and the equivalence transports universal properties of finite-limit cones in both directions.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence), clauses (1)-(4), applied as in the final sentence of the proof of Tag 03CI.

proof.text: Choose an isomorphism $\theta:e(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}h_U$. The functor on slices sending $p:H\to A$ to $\theta\circ e(p):e(H)\to h_U$ is an equivalence: apply a quasi-inverse of $e$ and its unit/counit to construct the inverse over $A$; the unit/counit identities over the bases follow from their naturality. Since the topology is subcanonical, $h_U^\#\cong h_U$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/h_U$ to $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)$. Its value on $(F,p)$ at $a:V\to U$ is the fibre $\{x\in F(V):p_V(x)=a\}$, with componentwise restriction. The composite is the required equivalence $\mathcal E/A\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)$. The site $\mathcal C/U$ is small since its objects and arrows are subsets of small sets of arrows and commutative triangles of $\mathcal C$; its covering families are exactly the underlying covering families by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 04GZ (lemma-localize-topos), proof via Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek); localized topology in Section 00XZ.

proof.text: The forgetful functor $v:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ is continuous: it sends a covering family to the identical underlying cover, and pullbacks of covering arrows in the slice are computed by the same pullbacks in $\mathcal C$. It is cocontinuous: given a covering family $\{W_i\to V\}$ in $\mathcal C$ and $a:V\to U$, the arrows $(W_i\to V\xrightarrow a U)\to(V\xrightarrow a U)$ form a covering in the slice whose image is that family itself. These assertions follow directly from [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction]: precomposition along $v$, namely $F\mapsto F|_U$, is the inverse image of a geometric morphism. Transport this adjunction through the equivalences of steps 3 and 4; composition of inverse images is as in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Thus the transported functor is a geometric inverse image on $\mathcal E/A$.

source.place: Section 00XZ (section-localize), localization functor; Tag 00XR (lemma-when-shriek), continuous and cocontinuous functors, and Tag 04GZ.

proof.text: Identify that transported functor explicitly. An equivalence preserves products by their universal property: maps from a test object into $e(H\times A)$ correspond, after applying the quasi-inverse, to pairs of maps into $H$ and $A$, hence to maps into $e(H)\times e(A)$. Composing with $\theta$ identifies the slice object $(H\times A\to A)$ with $(e(H)\times h_U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}h_U)$. Products of sheaves are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Therefore the fibre formula of [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] sends this slice object, at $a:V\to U$, to $\{(x,t)\in e(H)(V)\times h_U(V):t=a\}$. Projection $(x,a)\mapsto x$ is a bijection with inverse $x\mapsto(x,a)$. Along $b:W\to V$ both sides restrict $x$ to $e(H)(b)(x)$ and replace $a$ by $ab$, so these bijections are natural in slice objects and in $H$. Consequently the slice geometric inverse image is precisely $H\mapsto(H\times A\to A)$ and corresponds under the constructed equivalence to restriction, as claimed.

source.place: Tag 04GZ (lemma-localize-topos), inverse-image description; Tag 03EE (lemma-compute-j-shriek-restrict); explicit fibre calculation from Tag 00Y1.

proof_origin.place: Construction following Tags 03CI and 03A1 and the fibre calculation of Tags 00Y1 and 04GZ, with an explicit preliminary covering-family replacement because def-weil-pbc-topos allows arbitrary sieve sites.
